title: Consensys Plans to Spin MetaMask Into Its Own Company
summary: Consensys said it intends to separate MetaMask — one of the most widely used self-custody wallets — into its own standalone company, according to reporting on 9 September 2026.
blocks: Consensys said it intends to separate MetaMask — one of the most widely used self-custody wallets — into its own standalone company, according to reporting on 9 September 2026.

Structural moves like this are common as a product matures: a dedicated company can raise capital, set its own roadmap and focus on a single user base rather than sharing priorities inside a larger parent.

For users, day-to-day use of a wallet is unaffected by corporate structure. What matters for you remains the same: who controls the keys. A self-custody wallet means you hold the recovery phrase, and that responsibility does not change with the org chart.
